claim: A symmetric integral lift reduces the congruence problem to one infinite cyclic relation defect, while the proposed genuine scalar character is impossible because a metaplectic quarter-turn lift has fourth power equal to the nontrivial cover kernel.
embedding: one symplectic-pair block SL(2) -> Sp(4), with the other pair fixed

outcome.finiteC4ValuedScalarRoute: ruled out in the stated one-block genuine-character form
outcome.genuineEtaScalarRoute: survives with S_tilde -> zeta8 and K -> i, pending sewn-defect comparison
outcome.next: compare the sewn order-23 defect/Pfaffian phase on K with the eta value i; use a vector-valued kernel if incompatible

boundary: The no-go is for identifying the finite C4 values with a genuine character on the declared one-block embedding; it does not rule out genuine eighth-root scalar lines, vector-valued kernels or embeddings with different Maslov parity.
